title: Penalty for taking advantage with wrong order of play
question: If two players agree to play out of order so that one of them can get a clear advantage, what is the penalty?

choices.text: No penalty if they both agree.
Only the player who played early gets a penalty.
Both players get two penalty strokes.

explanation: If players play out of order to give an advantage, both get two penalty strokes. It doesn't matter if they agree.

juniorVersion.title: What happens if you both agree to play out of turn to help one player?
juniorVersion.question: If you and your friend agree to hit your shots in the wrong order so it helps one of you, what is the penalty?

choices.text: No penalty if you both say it’s okay.
Only the player who hits first gets a penalty.
Both of you get two extra shots added to your scores.
You have to hit your balls again.

juniorVersion.explanation: If you both agree to play in the wrong order to help one of you, both of you get two shots added to your score. It doesn’t matter if you agreed.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The order in which each player takes their turn to hit.
Extra shots added to your score for breaking a rule.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Let kids act out a simple turn-by-turn scenario to see what happens when they switch order and why it matters.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think there is no penalty if they both agree.
They may think only the player who played out of turn gets a penalty.
